name: Group Steiner Tree
problem_statement: Given an edge-weighted graph and a collection of potentially overlapping vertex groups, find a minimum-weight connected subtree that includes at least one vertex from every group.

normalization: Reject directed input unless an explicit undirected projection is requested.
Collapse parallel edges by keeping the minimum nonnegative weight.

problem_inputs.name: groups
problem_inputs.constraints: at least one group; every group nonempty; groups may overlap and may share vertices with each other
problem_inputs.description: Each group must contribute at least one vertex to the returned tree.

problem_inputs.name: required_vertices
problem_inputs.description: Optional vertices (e.g. single-terminal requirements) that must appear in the tree regardless of group membership; equivalent to singleton groups.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether a certified-approximation result (e.g. a 2-approximation) with a disclosed ratio is permitted instead of an exact minimum.

required_outputs.name: tree_edges
required_outputs.description: Edges forming the returned connected subtree.

required_outputs.name: selected_vertices
required_outputs.description: Vertices spanned by tree_edges, including at least one representative per group.

optional_outputs.name: group_representatives
optional_outputs.description: The specific vertex chosen to satisfy each group index, when a group has multiple qualifying vertices in the tree.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified worst-case ratio to optimal for an approximate result.

solution_semantics.objective: Minimize tree_weight over connected subtrees of the normalized graph that contain at least one vertex from every group in groups and every vertex in required_vertices.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true; approximate mode must disclose approximation_bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Multiple minimum-weight trees may exist; return one unless alternates are explicitly requested.
solution_semantics.ordering: tree_edges and selected_vertices are unordered sets.

validation_rules: tree_edges forms a single connected acyclic subgraph (a tree) in the normalized graph.
Every group in groups has at least one vertex in selected_vertices.
Every vertex in required_vertices is in selected_vertices.
tree_weight equals the sum of tree_edges weights.
Reported optimal=true matches independent verification against an exhaustive oracle on small fixtures.
edge_cases: A single group containing the whole vertex set reduces to the cheapest single vertex, with an empty tree_edges and tree_weight zero.
Groups that already share a common vertex may be satisfied by a single-vertex tree.
Disconnected graphs where some group is entirely unreachable from another group make the instance infeasible; this must be reported rather than silently returning a partial tree.
Overlapping groups may be satisfied by the same vertex without double-selecting it.

correctness: tree-weight agreement with exact oracle on small/medium fixtures
